content.intro: Learn conditional requests and http caching headers through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Conditional Requests and HTTP Caching Headers matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines conditional requests and http caching headers as part of middleware, cookies, sessions, and messaging. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: ETag; Last-Modified; Cache-Control; Conditional responses; Avoiding the caching of private user-specific responses. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Cache-Control
items.text: Cache invalidation and key scope are part of correctness. Include relevant variation dimensions, use a deliberate TTL, avoid cross-user leakage, and invalidate or refresh entries after writes.

items.title: Conditional responses
items.text: Conditional responses is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.
